title: Need "simple" helps on my first Game

posts.author: Escravamatsu
posts.body:
Hello!
I used RPG Maker during my teenage years, for fun, but I never worked with plugins or scripts. I don't know how to code, so I'm stuck with plugins and guides. Right now, these are the points I need help with.
-How to make enemy and player illustrations move (instead of a png, be a gif).
-How to add a super effective damage image if the player hits an element opposite the enemy.
-I'm using the VisuStella battlefront plugin that I bought, but I'm having trouble even with that, because I'd like to remove the character's face in the center of the screen and lower the menu to make the enemy area cleaner.
Below is the prototype of the game I'm making. I'm a professional illustrator, but as I said, I have no programming experience.

posts.author: Escravamatsu
posts.body:
Thank you so much!! I didn`t know about these plugins, have a lot!
Also, I was trying to search in this site but I didn`t find something usual. You know any plugin or method to make these sprites to animate?
Like, if I do 3-5 images of this slime and put them to appears in order to do a simple animation, just to not have static images.
Thank you again!

posts.author: Winshifter
posts.body: If you are already using VisuStella plugins, the BattleCore plugin from them already allows you to have animated enemies...I don't remember exactly, but the instructions tells you how to do it. Basically, you have your enemies in the same format as the SV battlers for your party characters and you place those files on the same folder. The instructions for that are in the BattleCore plugin, even in their sample project they have an example I think.

Sorry, somebody know more about it?

posts.author: Winshifter
posts.body:
That's because you are not using the proper format of for SV_characters, the instructions tells you that is the same format of SV_characters for sideview characters. The only thing you will have to take into consideration, is that you have to draw them front facing, not looking to the left as the default ones, but other than that, is the format of SV_characters. The format is on the Side-View Character Standards of the documentation on MZ. Help -> Contents -> Documentation -> Side-View Character Standards.
If you are only using one file for a particular enemy, just use the notetag  <Sideview Battler: filename>.
Basically, you don't get to choose the frames, those are already predifinded, if you need to have specific number of frames for animated enemies, then you would require a different plugin.
